MovieScript:
The golden hour settled over the quiet streets of Queens, stretching the shadows of Peter Parker and Mary Jane as they walked side by side.

"Peter, do you really think I have it?" Mary Jane asked, stopping near her fence. Her eyes held a flicker of uncertainty that she rarely showed the world.

Peter looked at her, his gaze steady and sincere. "I do. You were the star of every school play. I cried like a baby when you played Cinderella."

Mary Jane let out a soft laugh, shaking her head. "Peter, that was the first grade."

"Even so," Peter said, his voice dropping an octave, colored by a newfound gravity. "Sometimes you just know people. You can see what’s coming for them. And for you? You’re going to light up Broadway."

Mary Jane studied him for a long beat, seeing something in the boy next door that she hadn't noticed before—a quiet strength. "You know... you’re taller than you look."

"I hunch," Peter admitted, shrugging awkwardly.

"Don't," she whispered.

The moment was shattered by the roar of a high-performance engine. Flash Thompson pulled up in a gleaming new birthday present, his ego radiating from the driver's seat. With a hurried goodbye, Mary Jane vanished into the chrome and leather world of popularity, leaving Peter standing alone in the cooling air.

The interior of the old sedan was thick with a tension that hadn't existed between them a month ago. Uncle Ben kept his eyes on the road, his knuckles white on the steering wheel. As they pulled up to the library, he clicked the child safety locks.

"We need to talk, Peter," Ben said, his voice heavy with the burden of a father figure. "You’re changing. You shirk your chores, you’re doing those strange experiments in your room, and now... you’re starting fights at school."

"I told you, I didn't start that fight," Peter snapped, staring out the window at the passing crowds.

"But you sure finished it," Ben countered. "Listen to me, Peter. Flash Thompson probably deserved what happened, but just because you can beat him up doesn't give you the right to."

Ben turned to look at him, his eyes pleading for the boy to understand the weight of manhood. "Remember: with great power comes great responsibility."

The words felt like a lecture to Peter's stinging pride. He turned, his eyes flashing with a teenage rebellion that cut deep. "Are you afraid I'll become a criminal? Stop lecturing me! And stop pretending to be my father!"

The silence that followed was deafening. Uncle Ben’s face paled, as if he had been struck. He slowly unlocked the doors.

"I'll pick you up here at ten," Ben said quietly.
